purpose: When a canonical solution exists, competing non-canonical implementations lose execution authority automatically.
enforcement_rule: Before execution, MIM/TOD must check whether the requested implementation, route, parser, artifact, or objective is canonical, superseded, or competing with a canonical solution.

canonical_solutions.title: File-backed objectives dashboard runtime state
canonical_solutions.summary: Use runtime/shared file-backed objectives, escalation, continuity, and gate artifacts while database objective queries remain slow/unreliable.

canonical_solutions.title: Existing Capability Check before implementation
canonical_solutions.summary: Implementation-like objectives require a completed existing-capability check before creation or execution.

canonical_solutions.title: Operator-facing response synthesis
canonical_solutions.summary: MIM replies should summarize what changed, what remains blocked, what matters now, and next action without lifecycle or artifact leakage.

canonical_solutions.title: Material implementation proof gate
canonical_solutions.summary: TOD implementation completion requires material diff, relevant file touch, behavior validation, live-path proof when applicable, and regression evidence.

canonical_solutions.title: Freshness provenance and trust ranking
canonical_solutions.summary: Evidence freshness must rank live-path, validation, material diff, runtime state, and wrapper summaries separately so a new wrapper cannot hide stale execution.

supersession_records.reason: Database objective query path can hang; file-backed runtime state is current authority for objectives UI continuity.
Implementation work must check existing routes/artifacts/canonical solutions before execution.
Codex escalation requires structured context and lineage.
Implementation completion must prove material source/behavior change, not only publish wrappers.
Fresh latest artifacts must not promote stale source evidence.
